02 / The service

Choose how much of the vehicle to wrap.

Vehicle wraps use specialist vinyl film to change the appearance of a car, van or commercial vehicle. From our Norwich workshop, we design and fit partial and full wraps for Norfolk businesses that want more room for their branding and for drivers planning a colour change. A partial wrap uses selected panels or a section of the body. A full wrap covers most exterior body panels, with trims and door shuts agreed in the quote.

A printed wrap gives you room for photos, custom colours or a large illustration. A solid colour-change film is a different specification and is chosen for its colour and finish. We review the shape and condition of the bodywork before agreeing which film and coverage make sense. Send us photos of any stone chips, repairs or existing film so we can discuss preparation before booking.

If the van is a working vehicle, tell us which days it can be off the road and what the graphics need to do. We’ll show the planned coverage on a proof and confirm what is included before fitting in Norwich.

08 / Vinyl & materials

Choose the right film.

Cast wrap film is suited to complex curves and recesses. Printed wraps typically use compatible print film and laminate. Ask about the life of the specific product on the roof, bonnet and vertical panels.

Cast vs calendered
Cast vinyl conforms to more complex bodywork. Suitable calendered film can work on flatter areas and simpler curves. The exact product and surface determine suitability.
Brands used
3M and Metamark are examples to discuss. Ask for the product and finish on your quote.
Lifespan
Film, panel angle, care and exposure all matter. As one product example, 3M 2080 lists up to eight years on qualifying vertical applications and up to three on horizontal applications. Check the applicable product terms.
Finishes
Ask about gloss, matt, satin, chrome-effect or reflective film. Speciality finishes can have different fitting, care and durability requirements.

16 / FAQ

Good to know.

What affects the cost of a wrap?

Vehicle size, panel shape, coverage, materials and artwork all affect the quote. Photos and your make and model help us give you a more accurate estimate.

Can you wrap over damaged paint?

Send clear photos of any damage, corrosion or repairs. The team can assess the surface before agreeing the scope of work.

Can you wrap a van without doing the whole body?

Yes. A partial wrap can cover selected panels or a larger section of the vehicle. We confirm exactly what is covered on the proof and quote.

Are door shuts and trims included in a full wrap?

Coverage varies. Door shuts, roof, bumpers, textured trims and badges are discussed before you approve the quote.

What paint condition do you need for a wrap?

The film needs a sound, suitable surface. Send photos of flaking paint, rust, damage or repairs so we can inspect and advise.

How long should I allow for a full wrap?

Plan for several fitting days as a guide. Vehicle size, film, prep and the number of panels affect the appointment length.

Is wrap vinyl the same as paint protection film?

They are different products. Decorative vinyl changes appearance and adds a layer over covered paint. For stone-chip resistance, ask about paint protection film.

Can I wrap a leased vehicle?

Ask your lease provider for written permission and check its handback requirements before booking. Discuss professional removal and any paint repairs with us.

How long will a vehicle wrap last?

The life depends on the exact film, finish, panel angle, weather exposure, use and maintenance. Ask for the film specification and its applicable terms.

How do I wash a wrapped vehicle?

Follow the care sheet for the fitted film. Use mild products and take extra care around edges and seams. Ask the fitter before using a pressure washer.
